avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Probiotics (during acute therapy)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Vancomycin kills beneficial gut bacteria; simultaneous probiotic supplementation may reduce antibiotic efficacy or cause unpredictable bacterial dynamics
avoid_supplements.action: Separate probiotic administration by at least 2-4 hours from vancomycin dose; resume probiotics 2-3 days after completion of therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Nephrotoxic Supplements (Aristolochic acid, high-dose NSAIDs)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Vancomycin has intrinsic nephrotoxicity; concurrent nephrotoxic agents increase risk of acute kidney injury
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid nephrotoxic herbal supplements and limit NSAID use; monitor serum creatinine and vancomycin trough levels

caution_supplements.name: Electrolyte supplements (Potassium, Magnesium)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Vancomycin may cause electrolyte abnormalities; supplementation may complicate monitoring
caution_supplements.action: Obtain baseline electrolytes; use supplementation only if serum levels confirm deficiency

avoid_foods.name: High-sodium foods (if IV formulation used with cardiac/renal disease)
avoid_foods.mechanism: IV vancomycin formulations contain sodium chloride; excessive dietary sodium may worsen fluid retention in susceptible patients
avoid_foods.action: Monitor sodium intake in patients with heart failure or renal impairment; review IV formulation sodium content

caution_foods.name: Fermented foods and high-fiber foods (oral vancomycin only)
caution_foods.mechanism: May alter gut microbiota composition and affect oral vancomycin efficacy for C. difficile infection
caution_foods.action: Moderate intake of fermented foods during oral vancomycin therapy; resume after treatment completion

monitoring_notes: Vancomycin undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism and has low propensity for drug interactions via CYP enzymes. Primary monitoring focus should be renal function (serum creatinine, BUN), vancomycin trough levels (target 15-20 mcg/mL), and auditory function (ototoxicity risk), particularly when combined with other nephrotoxic or ototoxic agents.
